answer: Reputation-weighted resource draw: each identity's access to shared compute scales with its age and verified work history, so a fresh cluster starts near zero. Every new account also pays a ripple tax: a small fee that rises with how many accounts share its network fingerprint or funding source. This makes an atlas of thousands of identities cost superlinearly, since each added node both pays more and inherits less capacity. An attacker's per-identity spend climbs while output stays flat; honest actors amortize cost into a durable haven of earned throughput.
